clue.text: Place to trash Spooner's crooner's triumph?

indicators.note: Spooner's signals that the opening sounds of two words are swapped, as Dr Spooner reputedly did

parts.note: Bing Crosby was the famous crooner, so crooner's gives BING'S
a triumph is a win

explanation.surface: A question about the big moment of a singer, perhaps a talent show victory, with a hint of binning it.
explanation.walkthrough: Said aloud, BING'S WIN runs together as 'Bing swin'; swapping the opening sounds B and SW gives SWING BIN.
explanation.definitionFit: A swing bin is a household rubbish container with a pivoting lid, somewhere you throw waste.

clue.text: Bat that's amazing, controlling ball with no need for power

indicators.note: something controlling another holds it in its grip, so one piece wraps round the other

parts.note: WOW is an exclamation meaning that's amazing

indicators.note: doing without something means a letter is dropped from the word

parts.note: a pill is slang for a ball, as in a football

explanation.surface: Praise for a cricket bat so good it controls the ball effortlessly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'controlling' looks like ball control on the surface, but it means one piece holds the other; 'power' is just its abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: Cricket bats are made of willow wood, so the material stands by metonymy for the bat itself.

clue.text: Veto old and new President

parts.note: to nix something is to veto or forbid it

explanation.surface: An old veto overturned by a newly elected head of state.
explanation.definitionFit: Richard Nixon was the 37th President of the United States, so the surname names a holder of that office.

clue.text: Where to place rump left out of veal ragout

indicators.note: left out of means the letter for left is taken away from the dish

parts.note: a blanquette is a French ragout of veal in white sauce

explanation.surface: A recipe note on a cut of beef being omitted from a veal stew.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rump' looks like a cut of meat to go in the stew, but it means a backside.
explanation.definitionFit: A banquette is an upholstered bench seat along a wall, a place for sitting on your behind.

clue.text: Composer's book appearance not OK

parts.note: a novel is a book

indicators.note: not OK means the letters O and K are removed from the word

parts.note: a look is an appearance

explanation.surface: A composer's book is not well received.
explanation.walkthrough: Composer's reads as 'Composer is'. LOOK without OK leaves LO.
explanation.definitionFit: Ivor Novello was a Welsh composer and actor, writer of 'Keep the Home Fires Burning'.

clue.text: Plucky old US flier starting to glide into Hudson River area

parts.note: TWA was Trans World Airlines, a defunct US airline

indicators.note: into says the letter goes inside the abbreviation for the state

parts.note: NY is New York, the state the Hudson River flows through

indicators.note: starting to means only the first letter of glide is used

explanation.surface: A brave old American aircraft gliding in over the Hudson, recalling the river landing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Plucky' looks like brave, but it means sounding like a plucked string.
explanation.definitionFit: A twangy sound is the resonant note of a plucked string, hence plucky in a literal sense.

clue.text: It's a beast to get money off tax collectors!

parts.note: to tap someone is to get money off them
IR is the Inland Revenue, the former UK tax collecting body

explanation.surface: An exclamation that wringing cash out of the taxman is a monster of a task.
explanation.definitionFit: A tapir is a large hoofed mammal of the Americas and Asia with a short trunk, an animal.

clue.text: Source of thickness of Cockney school base?

parts.note: Harrow is a famous English public school; a Cockney drops the H
a root is a base or foundation

explanation.surface: A question about what lies at the foundation of a London school's slowness.
explanation.walkthrough: Cockneys, of East London, famously drop the H at the start of words.
explanation.definitionFit: Arrowroot is a starch used as a thickening agent in sauces and puddings.

clue.text: Lowball? In Strine, it's 'low ball'

definitions.meaning: to cut a house offer at the last minute, a lowball tactic
in Australian cricket slang a ... is a delivery that keeps low and goes under the bat

explanation.walkthrough: Strine is Australian English as spoken; 'gazunder' is 'goes under' in that accent.
explanation.definitionFit: In British property dealing a buyer who drops the agreed price just before exchange of contracts gazunders the seller.

clue.text: Light yellow bog, loose inside

indicators.note: inside tells us the second word goes into the first

parts.note: a fen is a marsh or bog
lax means loose or slack

explanation.surface: A description of pale-coloured marshland, with something slack in the middle.
explanation.definitionFit: Flaxen describes the pale straw colour of flax fibre, typically of hair.

clue.text: Victor gets a trophy, having nothing along the way to eliminate

parts.note: V is Victor in the NATO phonetic alphabet

indicators.note: along the way means the nothing turns up partway through the trophy word

parts.note: a prize is a trophy
O looks like zero, nothing

explanation.surface: A winner picks up a cup having had nothing to beat on the road to it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Victor' looks like the winner, but it is just the letter V.
explanation.definitionFit: To vaporize something is to turn it to vapour, destroying or wiping it out completely.

clue.text: Englishman can boast

parts.note: can and john are both slang for a toilet
bull is boastful nonsense

explanation.surface: An Englishman is able to brag.
explanation.walkthrough: 'can' looks like a verb, but it is the slang noun for a lavatory.
explanation.definitionFit: John Bull is the stock personification of England or the typical Englishman.

clue.text: Sparring, a form of strenuous exercise

definitions.meaning: ... (rhymes with cowing) is quarrelling, as sparring partners do
... (rhymes with going) is propelling a boat with oars, hard exercise

explanation.definitionFit: The same spelling serves both a quarrel and the sport of pulling oars, pronounced differently.

clue.text: Demonstrator follows remote broadcast, causing outburst from Sky

indicators.note: follows puts the demonstrator after the rearranged word
broadcast means scattered, so the letters of remote are scattered

parts.note: a shower is one who shows, a demonstrator

explanation.surface: A TV news item: a protester follows an outside broadcast, prompting a rant from Sky News.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sky' reads as the broadcaster, but it is the night sky.
explanation.definitionFit: A meteor shower is a burst of shooting stars across the night heavens.

clue.text: Cuckoo village nearly on top of county with no third man in field

indicators.note: in a down clue, on top of puts the first piece above the second
nearly means the last letter is dropped

parts.note: Midwich is the village in John Wyndham's novel The Midwich Cuckoos

indicators.note: with no means the following letter is taken out of the county

parts.note: Kent is a county in south-east England

indicators.note: third picks the third letter of the word man

explanation.surface: A daft village sits atop a county side lacking its third man fielder.
explanation.walkthrough: 'third man' looks like the cricket fielding position, but it supplies only the third letter of man. KENT without that letter leaves KET.
explanation.definitionFit: Mid-wicket is a cricket fielding position on the leg side, so it is a place to field.

clue.text: Building up sets in shy game

indicators.note: game means willing or up for anything, here signalling the letters are reworked

explanation.surface: Building up a lead by taking sets in a game played with a shy opponent.
explanation.definitionFit: Synthesis is the combining of parts into a whole, the process of constructing something.

clue.text: Doyenne somehow managed? That's about right

indicators.note: about means wrapped around, so the rearranged letters surround the letter
somehow signals the letters are put together in some other way

explanation.surface: A senior woman managed somehow, which is roughly correct.
explanation.walkthrough: MANAGED rearranged as GANDAME, round R.
explanation.definitionFit: A grandame is an old woman or grandmother, a respected senior lady.

clue.text: Cooler decoration having replaced MDF with e.g. granite

indicators.note: read as re-placed: the letters are placed again in a new order

explanation.surface: A kitchen makeover where fibreboard is swapped for stone, making a stylish improvement.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cooler' looks like trendier, but it is the fridge.
explanation.definitionFit: A fridge magnet is an ornament stuck on the refrigerator door, adorning the appliance.

clue.text: Given almost full protection in commercial

indicators.note: in tells us the guard goes inside the commercial

parts.note: an ad is a commercial

indicators.note: almost means the last letter is lost

parts.note: a warder is a guard, giving protection

explanation.surface: Something handed over with near-total protection in an advertisement.
explanation.definitionFit: Awarded means granted or bestowed, as a prize is given.

clue.text: Shylock's money heard to be shilling shy? Boo!

indicators.note: shy means short of, so the letter is taken out
heard to be means what follows is the sound of the word

parts.note: Shylock is the Jewish moneylender in The Merchant of Venice; the shekel is the Jewish currency
S is the abbreviation for the old British shilling

explanation.surface: A jeer at Shylock, reputed to be a shilling short.
explanation.walkthrough: SHEKEL said aloud can be written SHECKLE; dropping its S leaves the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: To heckle is to interrupt a speaker with jeers, as a boo does.

clue.text: Surfing novice in '09

indicators.note: in tells us the learner goes inside the year

parts.note: '09 spelt out is O NINE
L is for learner, a novice

explanation.surface: A beginner on a surfboard back in 2009.
explanation.definitionFit: Surfing the web means browsing the internet, being connected online.

clue.text: Communique rejected within parliament

indicators.note: rejected means turned back, so the letters are read backwards
within says the letters are found inside the word parliament

explanation.surface: A message turned down within the House.
explanation.definitionFit: An email is a message sent electronically, a modern communication.

clue.text: One gets on elaborate chair occupied by lady in garden

indicators.note: occupied by means the lady is sitting within the rearranged letters
elaborate means fancy or worked up, signalling the letters are reworked

parts.note: Eve was the woman in the Garden of Eden

explanation.surface: A fancy garden chair taken by a lady.
explanation.walkthrough: 'elaborate' rearranges CHAIR into ACHIR; 'occupied by' puts the lady inside it. 'One gets on' means a person who succeeds, not someone mounting a chair.
explanation.definitionFit: An achiever is someone who succeeds, who gets on in life.

clue.text: Praise of a kind knowing no bounds

indicators.note: having no bounds means the first and last letters are removed

parts.note: related means of a kind, akin

explanation.surface: Praise of some sort that knows no limits.
explanation.walkthrough: 'knowing no bounds' looks like unlimited praise, but it trims the outer letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Elate has an archaic sense of raising up or exalting, a stretch towards praise.

clue.text: Stores planes inside standard garages

indicators.note: inside puts the smoothing word within the standard

parts.note: marks are standards to meet
to sand is to plane, smooth a surface
to park a car is to garage it

explanation.surface: Stores aircraft inside, with standard garaging.
explanation.walkthrough: Marks and Sparks is the British nickname for the Marks & Spencer chain of shops.
explanation.definitionFit: Marks & Spencer is a well-known British chain of department stores.

clue.text: See 23
Fast and almost unhealthy pulse

parts.note: Lent is the Christian season of fasting

indicators.note: almost means the last letter is dropped

parts.note: ill means unhealthy

explanation.surface: Fasting and nearly ill, with a pulse checked.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pulse' looks like heartbeat, but it is the bean family.
explanation.definitionFit: A lentil is an edible seed of the legume family, a pulse.

clue.text: Beauty fair not opening creates mess

parts.note: a dish is slang for an attractive person

indicators.note: not opening means the first letter is dropped

parts.note: level means fair, even-handed

explanation.surface: A beauty pageant without an opener causes chaos.
explanation.definitionFit: To dishevel is to disarrange or make untidy, as hair.
